newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London recovered from an early slide to end mostly higher on bargain-hunting and reflected the firmer New York trend. Traders said the August certified stock figures released on Monday were low but within trade expectations. By the close, November stood US$4 down at US$1,530 a tonne but other traded positions were between US$1 and US$9 higher. Arabica futures in New York rose slightly as speculators squared short positions acquired during the market's recent slump to one-month lows, dealers said. Prices fluctuated within a relatively small band throughout the day, falling early on bearish open interest data before bouncing back to session highs. Key December rose 0.65 cents/lb, to settle at 105.35 cents, falling shy of key resistance at 106 cents. Spot September rose 0.85 to 116.10, padding its premium to deferreds. However, market observers believe that strong producer selling will continue to limit the upside potential.

USA - According to Complete Coffee Coverage, for the week ended September 7, roastings totalled approximately 310,000 60-kg bags, down from 315,000 the previous week and compared to 295,000 the corresponding period one year ago. Cumulative roastings totaled 11.640 million bags versus 11.400 million bags in the same year-ago period.
UNITED KINGDOM - London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) certified coffee stocks fell to 929 five-tonne lots in August from 1,174 lots in July.

UNITED STATES - Supplies of green coffee housed in US warehouses fell in August to their lowest level in more than seven years, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported. Green coffee stocks declined by 93,000 60-kg bags last month to 1.816 million bags, their lowest level since May 1989, the GCA said. Prior to the August figures, a recent low of 1.878 million bags was seen in November 1995. The port of Laredo, Texas, posted the largest decline. Laredo stocks fell by 104,000 bags to 275,000, the GCA said. Stocks grew by 93,000 bags to 704,000 bags in New Orleans, a leading destination for South American coffee. Warehouse stocks in New York barely moved, falling 2,000 bags, to 238,000 bags. In Miami, inventories declined by 18,000 bags on the month, to 173,000 bags. The latest decline was well within market expectations. Traders and analysts had forecast a draw of between 50,000 and 200,000 bags for August, with most anticipating a figure of under 100,000 bags.

FRANCE - Coffee imports in June 1996 amounted to 605,916 60-kg bags, slightly up on last year's 602,309 bags. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996 (January/June) up to 3.43 million bags, 5.3 per cent up on imports in January/June 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 amounted to 6.25 million bags, down from 6.61 million bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/June 1996 were Ivory Coast (417,900 vs 389,200 bags), Brazil (309,000 vs 451,100 bags), Colombia (294,300 vs 283,100 bags) and Uganda (282,000 vs 211,100 bags). Coffee exports in June 1996 reached 121,569 bags, up from 89,663 bags exported in the like period the previous year. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996 up to 622,230 bags, up 15.7 per cent on exports in the first half of 1995. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 1.07 million bags against 1.16 million bags in 1994. The largest markets for French solubles in January/June 1996 were Romania (52,100 vs 25,900 bags), Italy (38,500 vs 34,200 bags) and Belgium-Luxembourg (20,500 vs 21,900 bags).
